# Plugin And Platform Configuration Schemas

Status: generated reference
Audience: operator, plugin maintainer, developer
Owner: configuration source owners listed for each schema
Evidence: docs/generated/inventory/configuration-schemas.json; scripts/docs-configuration-inventory.mjs
Applies to: every plugin-registered configuration schema, pipeline-platform.v2, and the compact swarm configuration
Last verified: generated from the current source inventory

## Purpose

Before you change plugin or platform configuration, use this page to find the field contract for that setting. The generator uses all `configSchema` registrations in plugin manifests. It does not assume that a file named `config.schema.json` is the complete set.

## How To Read Field Evidence

| Meaning status | What the evidence establishes |
| --- | --- |
| `qualified-runtime-authority` | The inventory records a field-specific explanation and its implementation evidence. Read the row for omission, empty-value and failure behavior. This label is not a result from live execution. |
| `schema-and-runtime-authority` | The accepted shape comes from the schema, and the row identifies the runtime consumer. A schema declaration is not evidence that the runtime applies a default. |
| `structural-container` | This row describes schema structure. Child fields and collection rules determine the accepted configuration. The label does not establish a runtime default. |

The **Schema default** column gives the schema declaration. It is not a universal runtime default. Test-provider configuration can resolve schema defaults before validation. Stage, adapter and observer registration validates supplied values without that resolution. A consumer can apply its own fallback. Before you rely on omission or an empty value, read the field's implementation evidence.

Authority: [registration validation](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/949a217e6530f929d9e43e5398712fa49db91ef4/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/registry/configuration.ts#L42-L78) and [provider default resolution](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/949a217e6530f929d9e43e5398712fa49db91ef4/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/registry/configuration.ts#L102-L120). These rules apply to configuration validation before execution.

Overall shutdown races against ADAPTER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT. These rejections and abort signals do not prove that the underlying adapter work stopped. <br><br>Readiness teardown, rollback and late activation cleanup pass an abort signal. They still await the shutdown promise. An adapter that ignores cancellation can keep that cleanup pending. The inline schema declares boolean\|string for plugin values. The runtime separately applies this normalization to the selected plugin or environment value: Config resolution gives Redis the same value. Redis normalizes it as a boolean or trimmed lowercase text. For 1, true, yes, on, required, enabled, isolated, network-policy, network_policy or documented, isolation is true. Other values are false`.<br><br>Omission: There is no value default. When the two source values are undefined, the effective value stays undefined. The observer merges registration configuration, then service configuration, then hook configuration. A subsequently defined value replaces the previous value for the same key. The merge ignores undefined keys.<br><br>Null and empty values replace previous values. When the merged config.redisNetworkIsolation is not undefined, the observer uses it instead of env.REDIS_NETWORK_ISOLATION. Then the observer normalizes the selected value.<br><br>Empty value: The declared inline type still applies to plugin values. If a null or empty value reaches the resolver, it overrides earlier configuration and the environment before normalization. For an empty value, config resolution gives the Redis security-policy reader the same value.<br><br>Change effect: When the OpenClaw-to-Redis host observer next loads the configuration, a change to `$.redisNetworkIsolation` has the effect given above.<br><br>Failure: Missing necessary values or numeric errors stop observer config resolution. With a null JSON value, value.error access can fail before that Error is constructed. Failed JSON parsing gives HTTP plus the response status. ## How To Use This Reference

1. Find the schema registered by the provider, observer, adapter, or engine that reads the configuration.
2. Before you edit the authored value, examine fields marked `required`, branches, limits and defaults.
3. Use the consumer evidence to find how the runtime interprets the field.
4. After a schema or consumer changes, execute `npm run docs:drift:config:check`.

## Inventory Limits

- A schema gives the accepted shape and declared defaults. It gives no evidence that each runtime branch uses each accepted field.
- A manifest or package path identifies the source component. It does not identify an organizational owner when the repository does not declare one.
- An unknown consumer remains an explicit gap. Before you change that field, examine the implementation.
